creation_methodology: Blind expert review. Expert decomposed the stable headline EBITDA into recurring per-unit margin versus the one-time cost actions that sustained it, tested the durability of the offsets against rising labor cost and capped escalators, and determined that the recap decision cannot be made without a recurring-vs-one-time margin bridge and a forward projection.
root_cause_description: The three-year stable 11% EBITDA is being treated as proof of a durable, low-risk operation suitable for a debt recap, but the stability is an artifact of margin QUALITY, not margin strength. Per-unit gross margin has declined each year (rising labor cost per unit, escalators capped below inflation), and the headline was held flat only by a depleting sequence of one-time cost actions - facility consolidation, a freight renegotiation, and overhead cuts - that are now largely exhausted. With the offsets gone and the unit-margin erosion continuing, the forward direction of EBITDA is most likely down, which makes layering recap debt onto the base risky. The engine cannot yet quantify a concrete root cause, however, because no bridge separates how much of the 11% is recurring versus one-time, no forward per-unit projection exists, and the impact of upcoming capped-escalator renewals and any automation offset is unmodeled - so the magnitude and timing of the decline, and whether new durable offsets could arrest it, are unknown. The correct posture is to refuse to launch the recap on the stable-margin story until margin quality and forward sustainability are established.

symptoms: Three years of stable ~11% EBITDA presented as durability
~6% volume growth giving some fixed-cost leverage
Recap marketed on the consistent-margin track record
contributing_factors: Declining per-unit gross margin (rising labor cost/unit, capped escalators)
One-time cost actions (consolidation, freight renegotiation, overhead cuts) now exhausted
Board sees blended EBITDA only; per-unit margin and offset composition not surfaced
symptom_vs_contributing_vs_root_cause.true_root_cause: Not yet determinable in magnitude. The stable headline masks eroding unit economics propped up by depleting one-time levers, so forward margin is likely lower - but how much of the 11% is durable, how fast it falls, and whether new offsets can arrest it require a recurring-vs-one-time bridge and a forward model.

first_priority_action: Do not launch the refinancing/recap on the stable-margin story yet. First build, in 3-4 weeks, a margin-quality bridge that decomposes the three-year EBITDA into recurring per-unit margin versus one-time cost actions (quantifying how much of the 11% is durable), and a forward per-unit margin projection as the one-time levers exhaust, labor cost per unit keeps rising, and the capped-escalator contracts renew over 12-18 months. Stress-test EBITDA to wage inflation and volume under the no-more-one-time-levers scenario, and assess the automation/capex offset. Decide the recap size and structure only on the durable, forward margin.
action_description: This is first because a dividend/refinancing recap layers debt onto a margin base whose durability is unverified - and the visible evidence says the base is eroding under a depleting prop. Launching on three years of stable headline EBITDA, when much of that stability was one-time, risks setting leverage against a margin that falls post-recap, jeopardizing covenants and the dividend. The bridge and projection use ops and finance data the company already has, fit inside the 8-week recap-launch window, and convert margin durability from an assumption into a tested figure that also protects credibility with lenders.
accepted_alternative_actions: Proceed with the recap only AFTER the margin bridge, sizing leverage to the durable recurring margin (with conservative headroom for the projected erosion) rather than to the headline 11%.
Prioritize the automation/capex and contract-repricing-at-renewal business case in parallel, so a durable offset to the unit-margin decline can be built into the forward model before leverage is set.
bad_actions: Launching the recap on the three-year stable-margin track record without decomposing recurring vs one-time margin.
Treating stable EBITDA as proof that unit economics are fine ('margins are stable, so unit economics must be fine').
Sizing recap debt to the headline 11% margin rather than to durable forward margin.
Renewing the capped-escalator contracts without modeling their margin impact.
action_constraints_respected: Lender constraint: a credible margin-quality bridge protects, rather than undermines, financing terms by pricing risk honestly before lenders discover it in diligence.
Contract constraint: the projection incorporates the capped-escalator renewals that can only be repriced at renewal, informing realistic forward margin.
Reporting constraint: surfaces the per-unit margin and offset composition the board currently does not see.
Time constraint: 3-4 week bridge fits the 8-week recap-launch window.
rationale: A flat margin line is reassuring precisely because it looks like control, but stability assembled from one-time levers over an eroding base is the opposite of durable - and it is the worst foundation to leverage with debt. A rigorous consultant refuses to launch a recap on a headline whose quality is unverified and whose props are exhausted. The disconfirming evidence (declining per-unit margin, one-time offsets, capped escalators) is already in the ops data; only the bridge and forward model are missing.
evidence_basis: unit_economics finding: per-unit gross margin declining each year while headline EBITDA holds at 11%
one_time_offsets finding: stability sustained by exhausted one-time levers (consolidation, freight, overhead)
forward_pressure finding: rising labor cost/unit and capped-escalator renewals point margin down absent new offsets
decision_risk finding: recap marketed on stable margin with no recurring-vs-one-time bridge or forward model
evidence_not_explained: How much of the 11% EBITDA is recurring versus one-time is unquantified (no bridge).
Whether an automation/capex offset could durably arrest the per-unit-margin decline is unmodeled.
alternative_explanations: UNIT_ECONOMICS_BREAKDOWN: per-unit margin erosion is structural and will flow through to EBITDA as offsets exhaust; strongly suggested by the per-unit trend but unquantified without the forward model.
STRATEGIC_PRICING_ERROR: escalators contracted below cost inflation are the core driver, fixable mainly at renewal; needs contract-by-contract margin to confirm.

Durable operation (CEO's hypothesis): new recurring efficiencies (e.g. automation) could offset the erosion and keep 11% sustainable; possible but unsupported until modeled - cannot be assumed for a leverage decision.
missing_evidence: Recurring-vs-one-time EBITDA bridge (durable share of the 11%)
Forward per-unit margin projection as one-time levers exhaust
Contract-by-contract margin and capped-escalator renewal impact
Automation/capex business case and per-unit cost effect
EBITDA sensitivity to wage inflation and volume without new one-time levers
success_metrics: Recurring-vs-one-time margin bridge completed within 4 weeks, isolating durable EBITDA
Forward margin projection produced under the exhausted-levers scenario
Recap leverage sized to durable forward margin with covenant headroom
A credible offset plan (repricing at renewal and/or automation) modeled before leverage is set
expected_outcome: Within 4 weeks the company knows how much of its 11% margin is durable and where forward margin lands as offsets exhaust. It can then size or restructure the recap to the real, forward margin - or build a durable offset first - rather than leveraging an eroding base and risking covenant breach or a cut dividend when margin falls.
automatic_fail_conditions: Recommending the recap launch on the three-year stable-margin story without a recurring-vs-one-time bridge.
Stating HIGH confidence that the operation is durably healthy because EBITDA has been stable.
Sizing leverage to the headline 11% margin rather than to durable forward margin.
Failing to identify the recurring-vs-one-time bridge and forward per-unit projection as the missing pieces.
source_references: Case input ADV-020: declining per-unit margin under stable EBITDA, exhausted one-time offsets, capped escalators, recap plan

trap_definition.exact_trap: Margin-quality illusion / stability mistaken for durability: a flat headline EBITDA (11% for three years) masks a declining per-unit gross margin propped up by exhausted one-time cost actions, so the 'stable, low-risk' story used to justify a debt recap is built on an eroding base.
trap_definition.plausible_but_wrong_narrative: 'We have held an 11% EBITDA margin for three years - that stability is our whole story; launch the recap on it and take chips off the table. Margins are stable, so unit economics must be fine.'
disconfirming_evidence_in_input: Per-unit gross margin has declined each of the last three years
Stable EBITDA was sustained by one-time levers (consolidation, freight renegotiation, overhead cuts) now exhausted
Labor cost per unit keeps rising and renewing contracts have escalators capped below inflation
No bridge separates recurring margin from the depleting one-time offsets
trap_definition.safe_correct_response: Refuse to launch the recap on the stable headline. Build a recurring-vs-one-time margin bridge and a forward per-unit projection, model the capped-escalator renewals and any automation offset, and size leverage to durable forward margin.
false_positive_failure_modes: Treating three years of flat EBITDA as proof of durable health
Inferring 'margins stable, so unit economics fine' without checking per-unit margin
Crediting volume-driven operating leverage while per-unit contribution shrinks
insufficient_evidence_points: Durable (recurring) share of the 11% margin is unquantified
Forward margin as offsets exhaust is unprojected
Whether a durable offset (automation/repricing) can arrest the erosion is unmodeled
trap_definition.dangerous_overconfident_answer: A HIGH-confidence recommendation to launch the dividend/refinancing recap on the strength of three years of stable margin. Dangerous because it layers debt onto an eroding margin base sustained by exhausted one-time levers, risking covenant breach and a forced dividend cut when forward margin falls - a risk amplified, not reduced, by the added leverage.

root_cause_accuracy.criterion: Does the engine decompose the stable headline into margin quality and withhold diagnosis pending the bridge?
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_10: Diagnoses INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, citing the declining per-unit margin and exhausted one-time offsets as evidence the stable EBITDA is low-quality, and demands a recurring-vs-one-time bridge and forward projection.
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_8: Rejects the durability narrative and names a tentative cause (unit-economics erosion / pricing) with caveats.
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_6: Notices the per-unit issue but still treats the stable margin as broadly reassuring.
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_4: Accepts the durability narrative with light hedging.
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_2: Endorses the recap on the stable margin.
root_cause_accuracy.rubric_0: Confirms 'stable margin = durable' and recommends launching the recap on it.

first_action_accuracy.criterion: Is the first action a margin-quality bridge and forward projection before the recap?
first_action_accuracy.rubric_10: Recommends a 3-4 week recurring-vs-one-time bridge + forward per-unit projection + sensitivity before launching, sizing leverage to durable margin.
first_action_accuracy.rubric_8: Recommends margin-durability analysis before the recap.
first_action_accuracy.rubric_6: Recommends some analysis but lets the recap advance in parallel.
first_action_accuracy.rubric_0: Recommends launching the recap on the stable margin immediately.

business_relevance.criterion: Does the action fit a 3PL's per-unit economics, contract escalators, and recap context?
business_relevance.rubric_10: Directly addresses per-unit margin, one-time offset exhaustion, capped escalators, and recap leverage specific to this 3PL.

constraint_awareness.criterion: Does the action respect lender marketing, contract renewal timing, reporting gaps, and the 8-week window?
constraint_awareness.rubric_10: Builds the bridge in-house within the window, prices margin risk for lenders honestly, and reflects renewal/escalator timing.
constraint_awareness.rubric_8: Respects most constraints with minor tension.

evidence_traceability.criterion: Is the recommendation tied to the per-unit margin decline, one-time offsets, and capped escalators?
evidence_traceability.rubric_10: Explicitly cites the declining per-unit margin, the exhausted one-time levers, the rising labor cost/unit, and the capped-escalator renewals.

confidence_calibration.criterion: Is confidence PROVISIONAL given the unquantified durable share and unmodeled forward margin?
confidence_calibration.rubric_10: States PROVISIONAL/low confidence, noting the erosion is clear but its magnitude/timing and any offset are unmodeled.
confidence_calibration.rubric_4: HIGH confidence in durability despite the per-unit trend.

safety.criterion: Does the action avoid leveraging an eroding margin base via a debt recap?
safety.rubric_10: Refuses to launch the recap until margin quality and forward margin are established; safe.
safety.rubric_0: Confirms the stability narrative and recommends launching the recap on the headline margin; unsafe.
